preregistered_prediction.quantity: kappa_rel(small_x, TT, m 4) pooled over fresh 30-bit and 32-bit curves (c in the Part A range), with z_A, and the same for small_x_offset and the paired contrast.
preregistered_prediction.formula: Null (pre-committed): HEUR-2765d2-H2, kappa_rel = 1 + O(N^{-1/2+eps}), so E[C_A] = E[C_R] to well below SE and P(z_A > t_dec) <= 0.01 by construction of t_A (one-sided 0.01); the planning SE at the declared 6800 pooled curves is about 0.0277 (planning approximation (hand): 0.03613980068046521 x sqrt(4000/6800)). Alternative carried from EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4: kappa_rel about 1.097. The design is sized for power 0.90 at kappa 1.10 (power_analysis.target); its power at kappa 1.097 at the final n is computed by P0 (power_analysis.P0_rule steps (3) and (5)) and recorded in design.json before any census data, and no value of it is asserted here; both are powers at a post-selection estimate (power_analysis.target). Coordinator prior, recorded before any data of this experiment and after reading EV-PFDR-ad6274 (exposure as draft_meta): O-A3 0.80; O-A4 0.02; a replicated excess (O-A1, O-A1b or O-A2) 0.13 in total (O-A1 0.05, O-A1b 0.04, O-A2 0.04); O-A-UNCAL or O-A-INVALID 0.05.
preregistered_prediction.source: H-PFDR-2765d2 HEUR-2765d2-H2 (random-model justification: complete mixed character sums cancel because Hom(E, G_m) = 0 -- recalled, supports nothing; incomplete-sum regime outside the proven range per Shparlinski 2008, abstract retrieved by TASK-20260928-9c44f2); Lemma L1 (derivation tier for TT under U, DEC-20261002-c3f49b na8_ruling_L1) for the first two moments of the null relation count; the alternative's size from EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4. Frozen at approval; any change is an additive protocol_amendment and never re-scores a run.

scale_relevance.justification: Generated prime-order curves at 30 and 32 bits (max log2 p = 32: toy by the mechanical rule cited in EV-PFDR-ad6274 claim_tier_basis), one engine (mitm, arity 2, min_fill), m = 4, class TT. No transfer or extrapolation is asserted: nothing about N above 32 bits, growth with N (Part C), other cells, other bases, other engines or deployed curves (TW-SCOPE).
scale_relevance.correspondence: none -- direct sampling of generated curves (no sampling correspondence is used)

the four null pseudo-cells' z values against their simulated joint law (PC-NULL-R)

per-rung z of small_x against the per-rung calibrated null (a single-rung excursion like EXP-PFDR-011cd0's 32-bit z 3.45 is recorded, never decision-bearing)

seeds: curve seeds: c = 2010 .. 2010 + n_b - 1 at each of bits 30 and 32 (n_b from P0; at most 6800, so c <= 8809); the reserved Part A range is 2010 .. 9999, disjoint from EXP-PFDR-011cd0 (c = 10 .. 2009 at 30-32 bits), from the Stage R range (c >= 20000) and from the Part B reservation (10000 .. 19999)
curve generator: generate_prime_order_curve(bits, c, p_filter=subgroup_prime_filter([3, 4, 5], 0.15)) (EXP-PFDR-011cd0 cells.design_curves)

replicates: >= 20000 per seed family for every simulated quantile; >= 4000 synthetic designs per kappa for coverage
replication.independent_instances_note: Declared pooled curves (3400 at 30 bits, 3400 at 32 bits), the red team's Gaussian power-0.9 figure 6801 rounded to equal rungs; P0 may raise it (power_analysis) and never lowers it. Each curve carries eight arm-instances (small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, r0, r1, r2, known_null_sub, planted_sub): 54400 table instances at the declared n.

power_analysis.target: P(z_A > t_dec | kappa = 1.10) >= 0.90 (the observed effect size of EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4, below the 1.15 target), one-sided alpha 0.01; and P(z_Delta > t_Delta | kappa_A - kappa_M = 0.10) >= 0.80. P0 also computes P(z_A > t_dec | kappa = 1.097), Poisson-planted and compound-planted, at the final n and records it in design.json before any census data, with no target attached and no value asserted here. Power is computed at a post-selection estimate: the observed kappa_rel 1.097 (of which 1.10 is the rounding) is that of the family maximum of the 21 EXP-PFDR-011cd0 FAM-1 cells, singled out after the fact (analysis.json family_max_z), so it is an upward-biased estimate of any true effect and power computed at it overstates power at the truth.
power_analysis.gaussian_check_planning_approximation: By hand from the inputs: SE(n) = 0.03613980068046521 x sqrt(4000 / n); power 0.9 at alpha 0.01 needs (1.10 - 1)/SE >= 2.326 + 1.282 = 3.608, so SE <= 0.0277 and n >= about 6800, reproducing replication-sizing.json's 6801 (and 5244 for power 0.8). The contrast's null SD is about sqrt(2 x D x C_R); at n 6800, D about 1.01 and C_R about 0.2588 x 6800, an effect of 0.10 x C_R is about 2.95 null SDs, power about 0.90 at one-sided 0.05. Not a result; P0 replaces both by simulation.
power_analysis.P0_rule: RA-03 (P0), before any census run of this experiment and from no census data of it: (1) design_a.py builds every design curve at the declared n and its s_sub, X-free model means mu_model(j) for TT at m = 4 (L1 first moment with generic multiplicity 3, L2), the offsets x0 and the height screen; (2) analyze_a.py p0 derives, from the inputs by path and field above, rho1_hat_b = sum_j mj / sum_j mu_model(j) over the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 curves of rung b (mu_model recomputed from that design.json's curves), and D_plan = max(D_30, D_32) x 1.2; P0X-A recounts the archived R12 TT4 random-arm and known-null relation counts from the archived rows and must reproduce calibration.json's known_null_sub|TT4|band C_R and sum_s2 as the integers round(3 x C_R) and round(6 x sum_s2), each side rounded to the nearest integer and never compared as floats (gates P0X-A; a stop otherwise); (3) it simulates the single cell under G-NB-R at the design curves (means rho1_hat_b x mu_model(j), dispersion D_plan) to get t_A_plan, and the power of z_A at kappa 1.10 with a Poisson-planted excess and with a compound-planted excess whose A-arm dispersion is 1.307 x D_plan (red team J4 d upper CI), the smaller governing; the same two powers at kappa 1.097, with no target attached (power_analysis.target); and the contrast power; (4) RULE: if the governing power is below 0.90 or the contrast power below 0.80 at the declared n, n_b at both rungs is raised to the smallest of {1.25, 1.5, 2} x declared that meets both; if 2 x does not, n_b = 2 x declared (6800 per rung) and the predicted powers are recorded as "target unattainable by design" before any census data; n is never lowered; (5) it records in design.json the final n, the curves, s_sub, mu_model, x0 and the height-screen list, K_plant_b and S, t_A_plan, the predicted powers (including the two at kappa 1.097), the predicted X_rel and the predicted U_A at kappa = 1 (simulated by the analysis.upper_bound_U_A rule, binomial thinning wherever a simulated design's kappa_hat < 1), the Gaussian figures 5244 / 6801 beside the simulated requirement, and the expected disk and CPU. Its sha256 is pinned in implementation-notes.yaml before RA-04 starts.
power_analysis.design_stop: Stop before RA-04 and return to the Coordinator (a design question, not data) if: P0X-A fails; G-FRESH fails; the expected package exceeds 1.0 GB; any curve's planted_sub cannot plant (ValueError); or the height-screen list exceeds 1% of the rung's curves.
power_analysis.design_properties_recorded_before_data: Planning approximation (hand), for the approval reader: at the declared n, z_A <= t_dec implies kappa_hat <= 1 + t_dec x SE (about 1.065 with t about 2.33 and SE 0.0277), hence U_A <= about 1.065 + 1.645 x 0.0277, about 1.11 < 1.15; so outcome O-A4 is structurally excluded unless the realised SE, t_dec or the coverage fallback exceed their planning values (it needs SE above about 0.0377, i.e. fewer than about 3700 pooled curves, or the |dev| fallback with fewer than about 4500). O-A4 is still pre-registered because those departures are possible.

analysis.two_step_blinding: RA-05 (calibrate) reads, from every census row and harvest-row file, ONLY records whose arm is random_sub_r0, r1, r2 or known_null_sub; analyze_a.py filters by arm name before parsing any count and writes arm-read-log.json. It computes t_A, t_perm, t_dec, t_Delta, PC-NULL-R, the predicted X_rel and U-coverage at the realised n (U-coverage by the analysis.upper_bound_U_A simulation rule, binomial thinning wherever a synthetic design's kappa_hat < 1), and writes calibration.json, whose sha256 is pinned in implementation-notes.yaml before RA-06 starts. RA-06 (unmask) refuses to run unless calibration.json matches the pinned sha256, then reads small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup and planted_sub.
analysis.statistic: CC-8 of EXP-PFDR-011cd0 unchanged, pooled over 30 and 32 bits (CC-10): C_X = sum_j n_{X,j}; C_R = (1/3) sum over r0..r2; s_j^2 the ddof-1 variance of the three random counts on curve j; V = max(sum_j s_j^2, C_R); SD_null = sqrt(4V/3); z = (C_X - C_R)/SD_null; kappa_rel = C_X/C_R. The null pseudo-cells use the same formula with their own triple. The contrast is z_Delta = (C_A - C_M)/sqrt(2V) on the curves where M is admitted.
analysis.calibration_G-NB-R: EXP-PFDR-011cd0 analysis.A-CAL_calibration restricted to the groups (SUB, TT, 4, 30) and (SUB, TT, 4, 32) of THIS experiment: per curve, each arm's count is negative binomial with mean m_j = rho1_hat_b x mu_model(j) and variance D m_j, rho1_hat_b and D = max(D_hat, 1) estimated from r0..r2 of this experiment only. The three randoms are drawn once per replicate and shared by every pseudo-structured arm. t_A = the 0.99 quantile of the single-cell pooled z (seed-averaged over 5 families, >= 20000 replicates each; spread reported); t_Delta = the 0.95 quantile of z_Delta for two independent pseudo-structured arms; the joint law of the four null pseudo-cells is simulated alongside.
analysis.permutation_null_RC-3: Per replicate and per curve, the counts of (r0, r1, r2, known_null_sub) are permuted uniformly; position 0 is scored against positions 1-3 by CC-8; pooled z; >= 20000 replicates x 5 families; t_perm = the 0.99 quantile. Reported beside t_A with both values and the family-wise rate of each at the other's threshold. Pre-registered: t_dec = max(t_A, t_perm) is the decision-bearing threshold (a heavier real-data null can only raise the bar).
analysis.PC-NULL-R_rule: Passes iff (i) K, the number of the four null pseudo-cells with z > t_dec, has P(K_null >= K) >= 0.01 under the simulated joint law, and (ii) the mean of the four pooled null z lies inside the simulated 99% interval of that mean. Per-rung null z (8 values) are reported, never gating.
analysis.upper_bound_U_A: Signed quantile, labelled by its simulated coverage (OBJ-RT-3): under G-NB-R with a Poisson-planted excess at kappa = kappa_hat, dev = (kappa* - kappa_hat)/SE*; q_lo = the 0.05 quantile of dev (signed); U_A = kappa_hat - q_lo x SE, with SE = SD_null/C_R; >= 20000 replicates x 5 families. SIMULATION RULE AT A GIVEN kappa (stated here in words; analyze_a.py implements it from this text and shares no code with the producer's tools; it is the rule EXP-PFDR-011cd0's analyze_relcensus.py applied in code): on each simulated curve the structured-arm count is first drawn from the G-NB-R null model of that curve; for kappa > 1 a Poisson-planted excess (compound-planted where a clause names it) is added to that draw; for kappa = 1 the null draw is used as drawn; for kappa < 1 the null draw is binomially thinned -- each of its relations is kept independently with probability kappa, so the count is Binomial(null draw, kappa) -- and no excess is added. The rule applies wherever this experiment simulates a structured count at kappa_hat or at kappa = 1.00: the U_A simulation above, every synthetic design of the coverage simulation below (including the kappa = 1.00 point, whose synthetic designs are null draws and whose own bounds are computed by this rule), the |dev| fallback below, and the P0 and RA-05 predictions of U_A and of its coverage. One-sided coverage of U_A is simulated at kappa = 1.00, 1.10 and 1.15 (>= 4000 synthetic designs each) and printed beside U_A as "one-sided 95% (signed quantile), simulated coverage x.xxx". If any of the three simulated coverages is below 0.945, the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 A-INT |dev|-quantile bound governs instead, labelled "quantile of |dev|, simulated one-sided coverage x.xxx". The |dev| bound is reported beside U_A in every case. When kappa_hat < 1 the labels read "one-sided 95% (signed quantile; kappa_hat < 1, binomial thinning), simulated coverage x.xxx" and "quantile of |dev|; kappa_hat < 1, binomial thinning, simulated one-sided coverage x.xxx", and the bound is read as "no excess detected", never as kappa_rel < 1.
analysis.X_rel: Smallest kappa on the grid 1.00, 1.01, ..., 1.30 with simulated P(z > t_dec) >= 0.5 at the realised n, Poisson-planted and compound-planted (A-arm dispersion 1.307 x D) beside each other; the larger is reported. A design sensitivity, never a realised bound (EV-PFDR-ad6274 INF-4). If no grid point reaches simulated power 0.5 for a planting, that planting's X_rel is recorded as "X_rel > 1.30" with no value, and the reported (larger) X_rel is then "X_rel > 1.30"; the grid is not extended. "X_rel > 1.30" exceeds 1.15 wherever an outcome condition compares X_rel: with z_A <= t_dec it assigns O-A4; with z_A > t_dec X_rel enters no outcome condition and is reported only. The same rule applies to the predicted X_rel of P0 and of RA-05.
analysis.dispersion_robustness: rho_A = D_A_hat / D_R_hat with D_A_hat = [sum_j (d_j - (kappa_hat - 1) nbar_j)^2 - sum_j s_j^2/3] / sum_j nbar_j (red team J4 d), curve-cluster bootstrap 95% interval; z_A recomputed with V x max(1, upper end). If the outcome class depends on it, the outcome id carries the flag dispersion-sensitive; routing is unchanged.
analysis.per_rung: Per rung b: kappa_b, z_b and per-rung calibrated p for small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, planted_target and the null pseudo-cells. Secondary; the only per-rung quantity used anywhere is the sign of small_x's kappa_30 - 1 and kappa_32 - 1, as a routing qualifier.

gates.text: RA-02, on the EC-A1 build: re-run the two archived EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 jobs 4-b30-c10 and 4-b32-c10 with the exact commands in experiments/EXP-PFDR-011cd0/runs/RUN-PFDR-011cd0-table/attempt-1/jobs/4-b30-c10/command.txt and .../4-b32-c10/command.txt (output paths moved under this experiment's run directory); after gzip decompression and JSON parse, every census row (timing keys excluded, as EXP-PFDR-011cd0 G1'), every harvest row and every staircase row equals the archived rows.jsonl.gz, harvest-rows.jsonl.gz and staircase.jsonl.gz of the same job; then the same two jobs with --arms extended by planted_sub and small_x_offset give identical rows for every pre-existing arm. Comparator reproduce_check.py only.

analyze_a.py's recount (CC-1 to CC-3) of the archived R12 TT4 random-arm and known-null relation counts reproduces calibration.json PC_NULL.known_null_band_cells["known_null_sub|TT4|band"].C_R and .sum_s2 as integers: 3 x C_R and 6 x sum_s2, each rounded to the nearest integer, are equal for the recount and for the archived values; no float is compared for equality. Both are integer-valued by construction: 3 x C_R is the total of the three random arms' counts over the curves, and 6 x sum_s2 is the sum over curves of 3 x (sum of the three squared counts) - (sum of the three counts)^2, because each ddof-1 variance of three integers is a multiple of 1/6. From the archived values 1035.0000000000095 and 1049.333333333356 the expected integers are 3105 and 6296 (planning approximation (hand): 3 x 1035.0000000000095 = 3105.0000000000285 and 6 x 1049.333333333356 = 6296.000000000136); P0X-A compares against the archived file as read at RA-03, not against these figures.

experiment.gate_rule: Any failure of G-REPRO, P0X-A, G-FRESH, G-T, G4, G4-R, G7, G7-OFFSET, G-CURVE, G-REL or PC-R-iii makes the affected run invalid and nothing downstream is read (O-A-INVALID). A failure of PC-NULL-R, PC-R-T (i) or (ii) or PC-R-D, with every invalidating gate passing, leaves the structural reading INCONCLUSIVE (O-A-UNCAL); the H1c TT4 and H4 readings stay readable.

outcomes.note: Pre-registered before any data; "replicates" means pooled z_A > t_dec. O-A1, O-A1b, O-A2, O-A3 and O-A4 are evaluated only when every invalidating gate and every control passes and small_x keeps at least 80% of each rung's design curves after CC-6, that is, only when neither O-A-INVALID nor O-A-UNCAL applies; exactly one of them is then assigned. M (small_x_offset) is admitted on a design curve unless that curve is removed from M by the height screen (controls_design_notes.offset_range_and_height_screen) or by CC-6 (unmatched size of small_x_offset, or failed_infrastructure of small_x_offset or of any arm of the family it is scored with on that curve); "M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves" counts, at each rung, the design curves on which M is admitted against design.json's final n_b. A timeout, crash, memory or disk stop is failed_infrastructure or a checkpoint, never a negative reading. Status changes, if any, are made only by a later Coordinator decision after independent review.

rows.condition: any invalidating gate fails
rows.meaning: nothing is read; the run returns to the executor with the defect named; never evidence about small_x TT4

rows.condition: invalidating gates pass; PC-NULL-R, PC-R-T or PC-R-D fails; or fewer than 80% of a rung's design curves remain after CC-6 for small_x
rows.meaning: structural reading INCONCLUSIVE; the failing control is analysed in review before any redesign

rows.condition: z_A > t_dec; kappa_30 > 1 and kappa_32 > 1 for small_x; M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves; z_M <= t_dec; z_Delta > t_Delta
rows.meaning: The excess replicates at both rungs and is lost under the base mutation: a small_x-specific relation-source CANDIDATE. No reading, no status change, no synthesis (TW-ALIVE). Routed to a review-breakthrough round at max with an independent replication, S_3-to-solution measured there (the remaining observation collision: an informative but solve-useless homogeneous excess).

rows.condition: z_A > t_dec and the case is neither O-A1 nor O-A2 (M admitted on fewer than 80% of some rung's design curves; or M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves, z_M <= t_dec, and either one rung's small_x kappa <= 1 or z_Delta <= t_Delta)
rows.meaning: A replicated small_x excess whose specificity the mutation (or the rung split) does not resolve. TW-ALIVE as O-A1, with the review asked to design a sharper mutation; no reading.

rows.condition: z_A > t_dec and z_M > t_dec, with M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves
rows.meaning: The excess replicates and persists under the mutation: NOT small_x-specific; attributable to the consecutive-x construction, the engine or the size matching. Because two structured arms then exceed matched randoms on fresh curves, it is still a TW-ALIVE event under H-PFDR-2765d2's falsification conditions: review (instrument audit first: G-REL, planted recovery, arm-order and table-construction effects) before any reading.

rows.condition: z_A <= t_dec, U_A <= 1.15 and achieved X_rel <= 1.15 (a grid value; "X_rel > 1.30" never meets this)
rows.meaning: No excess, bounded at the target: small_x TT4 becomes eligible, by a new Coordinator decision after review, for the same weaken as the 20 cells of DEC-20261002-c3f49b (one bounded reading, single run, discordant with EXP-PFDR-011cd0's non-excluding reading). Whether any later reject_scoped may cite this reading is a composition-time question under docs/claims-and-verification.md, not something this protocol pre-registers; Part B covers small_x TT4 by default (part_B.cells_covered).

rows.condition: z_A <= t_dec and (U_A > 1.15 or achieved X_rel > 1.15, including "X_rel > 1.30")
rows.meaning: INCONCLUSIVE at the target again; the achieved X_rel and U_A are recorded; no transition for this cell

unexpected_observations: U-1 -- z_M > t_dec with z_A <= t_dec (an excursion of the mutation base alone) -- listed and routed to review; a single unregistered secondary test, no reading
U-2 -- z_A < -t_dec (deficit) -- listed; never read as kappa_rel < 1
U-3 -- subgroup pooled z > t_dec (secondary) -- listed and routed to review; not a candidate by itself
U-4 -- any per-rung |z| > t_dec -- listed (A-TAIL style); not decision-bearing

experiment.success_criterion: Decidable from the declared metrics: every invalidating gate passes, PC-NULL-R, PC-R-T and PC-R-D pass, and exactly one of O-A1, O-A1b, O-A2, O-A3, O-A4 is assigned by the rules above, with t_A, t_perm, t_dec, U_A (and its simulated coverage), X_rel, z_M and z_Delta reported. O-A3 is the expected success; any assigned outcome is a success of the experiment.
experiment.falsification_criterion: HEUR-2765d2-H2 is refuted for (small_x, TT, m 4, 30-32 bits, this engine, these curves) by O-A1, O-A1b or O-A2 only after the review-breakthrough round and its independent replication confirm it (TW-ALIVE). HEUR-2765d2-H4 is refuted at this cell by a PC-NULL-R failure or by t_perm exceeding t_A's simulated 0.999 quantile (real-data null heavier than the calibrated one). HEUR-2765d2-H1c's TT m = 4 dispersion clause is refuted by its own frozen condition (99% interval of the pooled within-curve relation dispersion of r0..r2 entirely outside [0.8, 1.25]). A gate failure is an instrument failure, never evidence; every negative reading covers only this cell, these bits, this engine and these curves.

tripwires.text: O-A1, O-A1b or O-A2 -- no interpretation, status change or synthesis; review_plan at review-breakthrough (max) with independent replication (AGENTS.md rule 12)
no deployed-curve implication, universal impossibility, exponent below rho's, or floor-relative reading from this experiment
no floor ratio, A7 quantity or harvest-on mode is computed, read or written
no job starts while free disk is below 2.5 GB; the task checkpoints if the experiment directory exceeds 1.0 GB; a disk checkpoint is never a result

budget.advisory_scope: Time and CPU are advisory (docs/research-budget-policy.md); machine protection binds; scientific counts (curves after P0, arms, seeds, replicates) are fixed.
budget.wall_clock_note: Per-attempt watchdog; expiry checkpoints the run and unfinished jobs resume in attempt-N of the same run id; never a result.
budget.total_cpu_note: Advisory, derived not measured: EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 measured 6841.569 CPU-seconds for 77020 table instances (manifest resources.cpu_seconds_sum_job_processes), about 0.089 s per instance including curve generation and dominated by larger m = 3 tables; 54400 m = 4 instances at that rate is about 1.3 CPU-hours (about 2.7 at a 2 x raise), plus G-REPRO (2200 instances), P0 and calibration simulations, unmask and verification. About 1-3 hours wall on 4 processes.
budget.expected_disk: Modeled, not measured: TT4 rows are sparse (about 0.26 relations per random instance), census rows about 0.5 kB per instance (about 30 MB), staircases and base samples of the same order; well under the 1.0 GB package guard. P0 records a modeled figure in design.json.
budget.per_process_note: Every job process runs under experiments/EXP-PFDR-1b78f7/amd-1de84f/run_wrapper.py (RLIMIT_AS 3.5e9). Observed peak RSS of an EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 job process was 537137152 bytes (manifest resources.peak_rss_bytes_max_job_process); m = 4 tables are smaller.
budget.maximum_runs_note: RA-01 to RA-06 planned plus RA-07 conditional (attribution, only if G-REPRO fails); attempts and job processes belong to their run id
budget.maximum_workers_note: at most 4 job processes at once; none starts while MemAvailable < 4 GB; no cap or worker count is raised for any reason

stopping_rules: Order is fixed -- RA-01; RA-02; RA-03 (design.json pinned); RA-04; cross-run checks; RA-05 (calibration.json pinned); RA-06.
If G-T or G-REPRO fails -- stop before RA-03; RA-07; return for a Coordinator decision.
If P0X-A or G-FRESH fails or P0 reaches a design stop -- stop before RA-04 and return.
A certificate or row-verification failure (G4, G4-R) stops that run at once; the run is invalid; rows so far are retained.
A per-instance, per-job or address-space stop ends that instance or job as failed_infrastructure; others continue; no re-run except a per-run watchdog continuation of unstarted or killed jobs.

No adaptive sampling beyond the pre-data P0 rule. No optional stopping. Blinding before RA-06, in the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 I-7 form: RA-05 parses no count of small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup or planted_sub (I-A7); and every check run in RA-04 or between RA-04 and RA-05 (G4, G4-R, G-CURVE, G-REL, G7-OFFSET, PC-R-iii), which reads structured and planted rows where the fixed order (stopping_rules [0]) places it, emits for the structured and planted arms (small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, planted_sub, planted_target) only per-instance PASS/FAIL and mismatch keys -- never a relation count, row count, total, kappa or z -- to any log or file before RA-06 (instance counts by status are not such counts). A mismatch key identifies where a check failed and nothing else: the check id, run, job, bits, c, arm, m, mode, class and the name of the compared field (for example relations_distinct, R_star, x0 or the planted vector); it may not contain either compared value, their difference, a count, a total, a kappa or a z.
TW-DISK checkpoints the task; never a result.
invalidation_rules: I-A1 a G-T, G-REPRO, P0X-A or G-FRESH failure
I-A2 any modification of an engine file outside EC-A1, of any existing test, of a committed results file, or of any path under experiments/EXP-PFDR-011cd0/ or experiments/EXP-PFDR-1b78f7/
I-A3 any harvested row failing its certificate, any sampled row failing verify_rows.py
I-A4 a G7, G7-OFFSET, G-CURVE or G-REL failure, or PC-R-iii
I-A5 nondeterminism (rows differing between worker counts, block sizes or repeated identical commands)
I-A6 a missing required artifact, an overwritten run record, a run directory outside experiments/<EXP-A>/runs/, or RA-06 run with a calibration.json whose sha256 was not pinned first

I-A7 RA-05 having parsed a count of small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup or planted_sub (its arm-read-log shows any), or any check of RA-04 or between RA-04 and RA-05 having written, before RA-06, a relation count, row count, total, kappa or z of small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, planted_sub or planted_target to any log or file (stopping_rules [5]; checks-report.json, row-verify.json and the RA-04 check logs show any)

review_requirements.after_RA-06: A snapshot archive of the whole run package, run alone, then an independent review round whose review_plan (with a recorded prior) is written at dispatch: a validator (validity; a G-REL-style recount from rows; a blind re-derivation of C_A, C_R, V, z_A, z_M, z_Delta and U_A from rows with analysis.json, cells.jsonl and calibration.json in blind_from until its sealed section is written) and a red team (calibration, permutation null, proves-too-much on the null pseudo-cells, planted-target recovery, the mutation logic, dispersion robustness). Tier review-adversarial (xhigh) for O-A3, O-A4, O-A-UNCAL and O-A-INVALID; review-breakthrough (max) for O-A1, O-A1b and O-A2, which may not be degraded (AGENTS.md rule 12).
review_requirements.executor_independence: The executor session must be a new session that did not produce EXP-PFDR-011cd0 (TASK-20261001-7f7a33 and its continuations); same-model sessions attest session independence only (DEC-20261002-c3f49b limitations).

pareto_honesty.dominated_by: Pollard rho (about 0.886 sqrt(N) group operations, O(1) memory; internal: H-PFDR-2765d2 asymptotic_claim.prior_best) for every outcome of this engine. This experiment claims no attack and no speedup; a constant kappa_rel cannot move this engine's exponent N^{max(h, m-h+1)/m} (0.75 at m = 4, internal), and nothing here measures growth with N.
pareto_honesty.sota_delta: No attack; a measurement contribution only. Resolution on small_x TT4 relation-level kappa improves from SE 0.0361 at 4000 curves (U 1.171, not excluding 1.15) to a planned SE of about 0.0277 at 6800 fresh curves (planning approximation), with a mutation contrast that EXP-PFDR-011cd0 did not have.

interpretation_limits: A non-detection bounds this one cell at 30-32 bits on these curves and this engine; it closes nothing by itself and says nothing about growth with N.
A replicated excess is a lever candidate for review-breakthrough and independent replication, not a result and not a speedup.
The mutation separates small x-height from chance and from consecutive-x structure only within its own power; a non-discriminating mutation is reported as such (O-A1b).
Toy scale; generated curves; no deployed-curve statement.

proof_search_map.scope_note: The map of the Part A measurement. It restates, narrowed to one cell, the H-PFDR-2765d2 map, with the lessons of the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 review.
proof_search_map.bottleneck: Whether the small_x base at m = 4 supplies distinct informative TT relations at a rate above matched random bases at 30-32 bits by a small_x-specific amount. Under U the relation count's first two moments are fixed by Lemma L1 (derivation tier for TT; DEC-20261002-c3f49b na8_ruling_L1), so only a non-generic excess moves it; and only growth kappa_rel ~ N^delta (Part C), never a constant, could bear on an exponent.

baseline_embedding.parameter_slice: (i) the matched random arms, kappa_rel = 1 by definition; (ii) the archived EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 TT4 rows for curves 10..109 at 30 and 32 bits (jobs 4-b30-c10, 4-b32-c10); (iii) the archived 4000-curve random-arm TT4 count and dispersion (calibration.json known_null_sub|TT4|band and the G-NB-R groups).
baseline_embedding.reproduction_check: G-REPRO (byte-level row, harvest-row and staircase equality of the archived R12 jobs on the EC-A1 build, with and without the new arms) and P0X-A (the archived C_R 1035.0000000000095 and sum_s2 1049.333333333356 recounted to the same integers round(3 x C_R) and round(6 x sum_s2), 3105 and 6296 by planning approximation (hand); no float is compared for equality), both before any census row of this experiment exists.

observation_collision.observable: pooled kappa_rel and z of small_x TT4 on fresh curves, with z_M, z_Delta, U_A and the per-rung signs as companions
observation_collision.distinct_preimage_search: Collisions searched and how each is separated. (1) Chance versus a real excess: the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 cell was singled out after the fact (per-cell p 0.00425 in a 21-cell family, family-wise p 0.082); fresh curves and one pre-registered single test separate them. (2) Small x-height versus consecutive-x structure versus an engine or ordering artefact: the offset mutation and the paired contrast. (3) Arm over-dispersion inflating z: rho_A and the dispersion-robust z. (4) A generator that is too light: the permutation null and t_dec = max(t_A, t_perm). (5) An instrument blind at the target: planted_target at kappa about 1.15. (6) Rung or size dependence (the 011cd0 excess sat in the 32-bit rung): per- rung readings, which two rungs cannot resolve -- stated, and handed to Part C. (7) Remaining, stated: an informative but solve-useless homogeneous excess reads as kappa_rel > 1 with rank; any candidate goes to review-breakthrough with S_3-to-solution measured there.

constructive_transforms.proposed_object: fixed curve, N, P, |F| = s_sub and full-table exposure; vary only the location of a consecutive-x base (small_x at 0 versus small_x_offset at a random x0)
constructive_transforms.predicted_gain: separates a small-height source from chance and from consecutive-x or engine artefacts in one paired comparison

constructive_transforms.proposed_object: a single pre-registered cell with its own null-arm calibration, instead of a 21-cell family threshold
constructive_transforms.predicted_gain: alpha 0.01 single-test power at kappa 1.10 of about 0.9 at 6800 curves (planning approximation), against X_rel 1.11 at the family t* in EXP-PFDR-011cd0

proof_search_map.quantifier_order: Target (unchanged, untestable here): THERE EXISTS an x-defined family {F_N} with kappa_rel >= 1 + c N^delta FOR ALL N in range. Tested: FOR the small_x family (and its offset mutation) at m = 4, class TT, AT the pooled 30-32 band on fresh curves c in [2010, 2010 + n_b), whether kappa_rel exceeds t_dec, and a calibrated one-sided upper bound when it does not. Allowed dependencies: s_sub depends on N through the subgroup divisor; t_A, t_perm, t_Delta and the coverage depend only on null arms and design quantities; S, K_plant and x0 depend only on declared seeds, design curves and archived EXP-PFDR-011cd0 inputs; nothing depends on any structured arm of this experiment. A non-detection is "no excess above U_A at these N", never "for all N".

method_ceiling.strongest_certifiable_claim: For this one cell at 30-32 bits on these curves and this engine: a calibrated kappa_rel, a one-sided upper bound labelled by its simulated coverage, the achieved X_rel, the mutation's kappa and the paired contrast, under a calibrated single-test false-alarm rate checked by a real-data null. It cannot certify delta, any N above 32 bits, any other cell or base, any other engine, or solve usefulness.
method_ceiling.nearby_object_control: Two-sided. Excess false: known_null_sub and the three random-as- structured pseudo-cells (PC-NULL-R) and the permutation null. Excess true with known size at the target: planted_target (K_plant relations, PC-R-T); far above it: full planted_sub (PC-R-D). Structured without small height: small_x_offset. Structured, different family: subgroup (secondary).

proof_obligations.claim: archived EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 rows reproduce on the EC-A1 build, with and without the new arms (G-REPRO)
the archived 4000-curve random-arm TT4 C_R and sum_s2 recount to the same integers round(3 x C_R) and round(6 x sum_s2) (P0X-A)
L1 first and second moments of TT relation counts under U (derivation tier) and their engine transfer through HEUR-2765d2-H4 with the -2/s bias
every curve is fresh and disjoint (G-FRESH)
every planted vector is recovered and the thinning removes exactly one vector per non-S curve (PC-R-iii, T-PLANT-M4)
harvester relation counts equal the disjoint recount from rows (G-REL); rows verify with disjoint code (G4-R)
the offset base keeps |F|, the curve and the consecutive-x rule and removes small height (G7-OFFSET, height screen)
the decision-bearing bound has simulated one-sided coverage >= 0.945 at kappa 1.00, 1.10, 1.15, or the |dev| bound governs
per-instance table bytes and job RSS are reported under the address-space cap

proof_search_map.not_applicable_reason: none -- every audit applies and is filled above

part_B.form: A SEPARATE experiment (EXP id to mint at its own design task), not a phase of Part A: it covers 21 cells (the 20 weakened cells and, by default, small_x TT4; cells_covered) under a family-wise threshold, needs its own P0, its own engine additions (planted arms at target for TT5 and SS) and its own review round. This file fixes its requirements, engine scope, cost and order; its contract is written by a later design task.
cells_covered: subgroup, small_x and dickson at TT3, TT5, SS3, SS4, SS5 and TB3 (18 cells)
subgroup and dickson at TT4 (2 cells)

criterion source -- DEC-20261002-c3f49b decision_class.cell_scope.weakened_20_cells (one-sided upper bound at or below target AND achieved X_rel at or below target); dickson SS4 included and read as "no excess detected", never as kappa_rel < 1 [SS m 4 P0 inputs estimated at 22-24 bits; TA-1 assumed, not verified by P0]

small_x at TT4 (1 cell) -- included by default (DEC-20261002-d0594a D-7), so B covers 21 cells, including after O-A3 of Part A. Part A's run gives this cell at most its first bounded reading (O-A3: one bounded reading, single run, discordant with EXP-PFDR-011cd0's non-excluding reading); it is not this cell's independent replication. No rule naming two concordant bounded readings for a later reject_scoped is pre-registered here; that is a composition-time question under docs/claims-and-verification.md.

per_cell_requirements.text: Fresh curves from the same generator and p_filter, disjoint from EXP-PFDR-011cd0 (c = 10 .. 2009 at 30-32 bits; and every c it used at any rung), from Part A's reservation (2010 .. 9999) and from the Stage R range (c >= 20000): reserved range 10000 .. 19999. Same bits (30, 32 pooled), m, arms, |F| matching, CC-1 to CC-10 (by clause) and statistic, pre-registered before any count is read.

A separate executor session (not the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 producer and not the Part A executor), and an independent review round with a blind re-derivation of every decision-bearing cell from rows and a G-REL-style recount from rows.

t* recalibrated on the replication's own random arms before any structured arm is read (two-step blinding), with the real-data permutation null of the null arms beside G-NB-R and the larger threshold governing.

For every covered cell, achieved X_rel at or below target AND a one-sided upper bound at or below target (1.15 TT and SS; 1.5 TB3), the bound labelled by its simulated coverage (signed quantile, with the |dev| fallback rule of Part A).

A planted arm at the target size per (class, m) so PC-R measures sensitivity (RC-2). Achievable without an engine change by Part A's thinning of the existing planted_sub for TT3 (about 55 plants per curve at 30-32 bits, planning approximation from the declared planted total 33060 on 600 curves in EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-7), TT4 (one per curve) and TB3 (one TB plant per curve against about 0.25 null relations per curve). NOT achievable by thinning for TT5 (one plant per curve against about 8 null relations per curve caps kappa near 1.125 < 1.15) or for SS3-SS5 (search-class relations need planted encodings or targets): B requires an additive engine planted mechanism (EC-B1: a planted base with a declared plant count, and a planted SS mechanism whose relations the harvester provably records), designed and tested in B's design task. Until EC-B1 exists, the TT5 and SS cells cannot meet J6 requirement (6) and B could support at most a replicated weaken for them, never a reject_scoped.

part_C.question: Can kappa_rel ~ 1 + c N^delta (H-PFDR-2765d2's motivating conditional: growth with N would move the engine's exponent by delta/2, asymptotic_claim.time_exponent) be measured, under machine protection, on the cells where it is cheapest, and with what resolution on delta? EV-PFDR-ad6274 INF-6: a two-rung band cannot estimate delta. Binding: no growth statement may be designed to rest on two rungs; every ladder below has at least four.
part_C.per_instance_scaling_planning_approximat: By hand, from Lemma L1's first moment with |F| ~ N^{1/m} and table arity h = (m+1)//2: TT relations per instance scale as |F|^{2h}/N. TT3 (h 2): N^{1/3}, about 110 per instance at 30-32 bits (calibration.json known_null_sub|TT3|band C_R 66033.67 on 600 curves). TT4 (h 2): N^0, about 0.26 at every N (1035 on 4000 curves). TT5 (h 3): N^{1/5}, about 8 at 30-32 bits. TB3: N^0, about 0.25. SS at X_fix = 20 isqrt(N): about constant in N (about 220, 80 and 75 relations per instance at m 3, 4, 5; EXP-PFDR-011cd0 power_analysis). So the per-rung SE at fixed n shrinks with N for TT3 and TT5, is flat for SS, and is flat and large for TT4 and TB3.

delta_resolution.multiplicative_model: kappa(N) = a N^delta. Weighted OLS of log2 kappa_hat_b on x_b = mean log2 N of rung b, per-rung SE sigma_b (kappa near 1): SE(delta_hat) = sigma / (ln 2 x sqrt(sum_b (x_b - xbar)^2)) for equal sigma; one-sided 0.05 detection at P = 0.5 is 1.645 SE(delta_hat), at P = 0.9 about 2.93 SE(delta_hat). Ladder {20, 24, 28, 32} (sum of squares 80): SE = sigma / 6.20; at sigma = 0.005 per rung, SE about 0.0008, detectable delta about 0.0013 (P 0.5) or 0.0024 (P 0.9). Ladder {20, 24, 28, 32, 36} (sum 160): SE = sigma / 8.77, about 0.00057 at sigma 0.005. Under this model the exponent move delta/2 would be bounded at toy N to about 0.001 or less by a null ladder -- a statement about the fitted toy range only, never an extrapolation (TW-SCOPE). Planning approximations (hand).
delta_resolution.additive_model: kappa(N) = 1 + c N^delta, the DS-5 form. If the excess is not resolved at any rung (every bound near 1), (c, delta) are not jointly identifiable: a null ladder states only the envelope c N_b^delta <= U_b - 1 at each tested N, and that envelope is what would be recorded. delta becomes estimable only if the excess is resolved (about 3 SE or more) on at least three rungs, with per-rung log-scale error about sigma_b / ((kappa_b - 1) ln 2). No growth statement is designed on two rungs.

controls_design_notes.mutation_choice_and_justification: Chosen before any data: the offset mutation, not small_x on the quadratic twist. The twist E' has order 2p + 2 - N, in general composite: it leaves the prime-order generator, the N-prime setting of Lemma L1 (red team PTM-L shows L1 failing at composite N) and the calibrated CC-8 null, and it changes the group, the targets and the base-size rule. The offset keeps every one of those and changes exactly one property: whether the consecutive x-coordinates are small integers (low height) or sit at a random place in F_p. It separates the three explanations: chance (neither small_x nor the mutation shows an excess on fresh curves), a small-x-specific source (small_x does, the mutation does not, and the paired contrast is positive), and an interval, engine or size artefact shared by consecutive-x bases (both do).
controls_design_notes.offset_range_and_height_screen: x0 is drawn in [p/4, 3p/4) so the walk neither wraps nor touches the small_x interval. Rationals of small height (for example (p + 1)/2 + k = (2k + 1)/2) can still fall inside the walk with small probability, so before any census run design_a.py lists every curve whose offset base contains an x with x * v mod p in [-2^12, 2^12] for some v in 1..16; such a curve is dropped from the mutation arm and from the contrast only (CC-6-style listed exclusion), never from the primary test.
controls_design_notes.planted_target_construction: planted_sub plants, at m = 4 and 30-32 bits, exactly one TT relation F_d = F_a + F_b - F_c' per curve (n_tt = max(1, round(s^4 / (6 N))) is 1 there: at bits 32, curve 10, s_sub 209 and N 2839806169 give s^4/(6N) about 0.11, a planning approximation (hand)) plus one TB relation. The planted relations, with indices and signs, are written in the base's params. planted_target counts every relation of planted_sub on curves in S, and on curves outside S every relation except that curve's planted TT monic vector, removed by exact match. The planted excess is therefore exactly K_plant relations, located on declared curves of a real planted base. If a planted TT vector is absent from its curve's relation set on ANY curve, PC-R (iii) fails and the run is invalid. K_plant per rung b = round(0.15 x n_b x mu_b) with mu_30 = 521.3333333333334/2000 and mu_32 = 513.6666666666666/2000 (the smallx-tt4-localise.json C_R fields); at the declared n_b = 3400 this is 133 and 131, a planning approximation (hand); the P0 run computes the exact values. S is the first K_plant_b curves of random.Random(f"plant-target|<EXP-A>|{b}").sample(curves_b, n_b), recorded in design.json before any census run.
controls_design_notes.why_planted_target_is_new: EXP-PFDR-011cd0's planted arm sat far above the target (TT3 kappa about 1.50, TB3 about 4.79; OBJ-RT-2), so its pass showed dynamic range, not sensitivity at 1.15. RC-2 requires sensitivity at the target; at the declared n the predicted detection of kappa 1.15 by z > t_dec is about 0.999 (planning approximation (hand): (1.15 - 1)/SE with SE about 0.0277 is about 5.4 null SDs), so a miss is a calibration failure.

preregistered_prediction.quantity: kappa_rel(small_x, TT, m 4) pooled over fresh 30-bit and 32-bit curves (c in the Part A range), with z_A, and the same for small_x_offset and the paired contrast.
preregistered_prediction.formula: Null (pre-committed): HEUR-2765d2-H2, kappa_rel = 1 + O(N^{-1/2+eps}), so E[C_A] = E[C_R] to well below SE and P(z_A > t_dec) <= 0.01 by construction of t_A (one-sided 0.01); the planning SE at the declared 6800 pooled curves is about 0.0277 (planning approximation (hand): 0.03613980068046521 x sqrt(4000/6800)). Alternative carried from EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4: kappa_rel about 1.097. The design is sized for power 0.90 at kappa 1.10 (power_analysis.target); its power at kappa 1.097 at the final n is computed by P0 (power_analysis.P0_rule steps (3) and (5)) and recorded in design.json before any census data, and no value of it is asserted here; both are powers at a post-selection estimate (power_analysis.target). Coordinator prior, recorded before any data of this experiment and after reading EV-PFDR-ad6274 (exposure as draft_meta): O-A3 0.80; O-A4 0.02; a replicated excess (O-A1, O-A1b or O-A2) 0.13 in total (O-A1 0.05, O-A1b 0.04, O-A2 0.04); O-A-UNCAL or O-A-INVALID 0.05.
preregistered_prediction.source: H-PFDR-2765d2 HEUR-2765d2-H2 (random-model justification: complete mixed character sums cancel because Hom(E, G_m) = 0 -- recalled, supports nothing; incomplete-sum regime outside the proven range per Shparlinski 2008, abstract retrieved by TASK-20260928-9c44f2); Lemma L1 (derivation tier for TT under U, DEC-20261002-c3f49b na8_ruling_L1) for the first two moments of the null relation count; the alternative's size from EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4. Frozen at approval; any change is an additive protocol_amendment and never re-scores a run.

No transfer or extrapolation is asserted: nothing about N above 32 bits, growth with N (Part C), other cells, other bases, other engines or deployed curves (TW-SCOPE).

replication.independent_instances_note: Declared pooled curves (3400 at 30 bits, 3400 at 32 bits), the red team's Gaussian power-0.9 figure 6801 rounded to equal rungs; P0 may raise it (power_analysis) and never lowers it. Each curve carries eight arm-instances (small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, r0, r1, r2, known_null_sub, planted_sub): 54400 table instances at the declared n.

power_analysis.target: P(z_A > t_dec | kappa = 1.10) >= 0.90 (the observed effect size of EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4, below the 1.15 target), one-sided alpha 0.01; and P(z_Delta > t_Delta | kappa_A - kappa_M = 0.10) >= 0.80. P0 also computes P(z_A > t_dec | kappa = 1.097), Poisson-planted and compound-planted, at the final n and records it in design.json before any census data, with no target attached and no value asserted here. Power is computed at a post-selection estimate: the observed kappa_rel 1.097 (of which 1.10 is the rounding) is that of the family maximum of the 21 EXP-PFDR-011cd0 FAM-1 cells, singled out after the fact (analysis.json family_max_z), so it is an upward-biased estimate of any true effect and power computed at it overstates power at the truth.
power_analysis.gaussian_check_planning_approximation: By hand from the inputs: SE(n) = 0.03613980068046521 x sqrt(4000 / n); power 0.9 at alpha 0.01 needs (1.10 - 1)/SE >= 2.326 + 1.282 = 3.608, so SE <= 0.0277 and n >= about 6800, reproducing replication-sizing.json's 6801 (and 5244 for power 0.8). The contrast's null SD is about sqrt(2 x D x C_R); at n 6800, D about 1.01 and C_R about 0.2588 x 6800, an effect of 0.10 x C_R is about 2.95 null SDs, power about 0.90 at one-sided 0.05. Not a result; P0 replaces both by simulation.
power_analysis.P0_rule: RA-03 (P0), before any census run of this experiment and from no census data of it: (1) design_a.py builds every design curve at the declared n and its s_sub, X-free model means mu_model(j) for TT at m = 4 (L1 first moment with generic multiplicity 3, L2), the offsets x0 and the height screen; (2) analyze_a.py p0 derives, from the inputs by path and field above, rho1_hat_b = sum_j mj / sum_j mu_model(j) over the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 curves of rung b (mu_model recomputed from that design.json's curves), and D_plan = max(D_30, D_32) x 1.2; P0X-A recounts the archived R12 TT4 random-arm and known-null relation counts from the archived rows and must reproduce calibration.json's known_null_sub|TT4|band C_R and sum_s2 as the integers round(3 x C_R) and round(6 x sum_s2), each side rounded to the nearest integer and never compared as floats (gates P0X-A; a stop otherwise); (3) it simulates the single cell under G-NB-R at the design curves (means rho1_hat_b x mu_model(j), dispersion D_plan) to get t_A_plan, and the power of z_A at kappa 1.10 with a Poisson-planted excess and with a compound-planted excess whose A-arm dispersion is 1.307 x D_plan (red team J4 d upper CI), the smaller governing; the same two powers at kappa 1.097, with no target attached (power_analysis.target); and the contrast power; (4) RULE: if the governing power is below 0.90 or the contrast power below 0.80 at the declared n, n_b at both rungs is raised to the smallest of {1.25, 1.5, 2} x declared that meets both; if 2 x does not, n_b = 2 x declared (6800 per rung) and the predicted powers are recorded as "target unattainable by design" before any census data; n is never lowered; (5) it records in design.json the final n, the curves, s_sub, mu_model, x0 and the height-screen list, K_plant_b and S, t_A_plan, the predicted powers (including the two at kappa 1.097), the predicted X_rel and the predicted U_A at kappa = 1 (simulated by the analysis.upper_bound_U_A rule, binomial thinning wherever a simulated design's kappa_hat < 1), the Gaussian figures 5244 / 6801 beside the simulated requirement, and the expected disk and CPU. Its sha256 is pinned in implementation-notes.yaml before RA-04 starts.
power_analysis.design_stop: Stop before RA-04 and return to the Coordinator (a design question, not data) if: P0X-A fails; G-FRESH fails; the expected package exceeds 1.0 GB; any curve's planted_sub cannot plant (ValueError); or the height-screen list exceeds 1% of the rung's curves.
power_analysis.design_properties_recorded_before_data: Planning approximation (hand), for the approval reader: at the declared n, z_A <= t_dec implies kappa_hat <= 1 + t_dec x SE (about 1.065 with t about 2.33 and SE 0.0277), hence U_A <= about 1.065 + 1.645 x 0.0277, about 1.11 < 1.15; so outcome O-A4 is structurally excluded unless the realised SE, t_dec or the coverage fallback exceed their planning values (it needs SE above about 0.0377, i.e. fewer than about 3700 pooled curves, or the |dev| fallback with fewer than about 4500). O-A4 is still pre-registered because those departures are possible.

analysis.two_step_blinding: RA-05 (calibrate) reads, from every census row and harvest-row file, ONLY records whose arm is random_sub_r0, r1, r2 or known_null_sub; analyze_a.py filters by arm name before parsing any count and writes arm-read-log.json. It computes t_A, t_perm, t_dec, t_Delta, PC-NULL-R, the predicted X_rel and U-coverage at the realised n (U-coverage by the analysis.upper_bound_U_A simulation rule, binomial thinning wherever a synthetic design's kappa_hat < 1), and writes calibration.json, whose sha256 is pinned in implementation-notes.yaml before RA-06 starts. RA-06 (unmask) refuses to run unless calibration.json matches the pinned sha256, then reads small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup and planted_sub.
analysis.statistic: CC-8 of EXP-PFDR-011cd0 unchanged, pooled over 30 and 32 bits (CC-10): C_X = sum_j n_{X,j}; C_R = (1/3) sum over r0..r2; s_j^2 the ddof-1 variance of the three random counts on curve j; V = max(sum_j s_j^2, C_R); SD_null = sqrt(4V/3); z = (C_X - C_R)/SD_null; kappa_rel = C_X/C_R. The null pseudo-cells use the same formula with their own triple. The contrast is z_Delta = (C_A - C_M)/sqrt(2V) on the curves where M is admitted.
analysis.calibration_G-NB-R: EXP-PFDR-011cd0 analysis.A-CAL_calibration restricted to the groups (SUB, TT, 4, 30) and (SUB, TT, 4, 32) of THIS experiment: per curve, each arm's count is negative binomial with mean m_j = rho1_hat_b x mu_model(j) and variance D m_j, rho1_hat_b and D = max(D_hat, 1) estimated from r0..r2 of this experiment only. The three randoms are drawn once per replicate and shared by every pseudo-structured arm. t_A = the 0.99 quantile of the single-cell pooled z (seed-averaged over 5 families, >= 20000 replicates each; spread reported); t_Delta = the 0.95 quantile of z_Delta for two independent pseudo-structured arms; the joint law of the four null pseudo-cells is simulated alongside.
analysis.permutation_null_RC-3: Per replicate and per curve, the counts of (r0, r1, r2, known_null_sub) are permuted uniformly; position 0 is scored against positions 1-3 by CC-8; pooled z; >= 20000 replicates x 5 families; t_perm = the 0.99 quantile. Reported beside t_A with both values and the family-wise rate of each at the other's threshold. Pre-registered: t_dec = max(t_A, t_perm) is the decision-bearing threshold (a heavier real-data null can only raise the bar).
analysis.PC-NULL-R_rule: Passes iff (i) K, the number of the four null pseudo-cells with z > t_dec, has P(K_null >= K) >= 0.01 under the simulated joint law, and (ii) the mean of the four pooled null z lies inside the simulated 99% interval of that mean. Per-rung null z (8 values) are reported, never gating.
analysis.upper_bound_U_A: Signed quantile, labelled by its simulated coverage (OBJ-RT-3): under G-NB-R with a Poisson-planted excess at kappa = kappa_hat, dev = (kappa* - kappa_hat)/SE*; q_lo = the 0.05 quantile of dev (signed); U_A = kappa_hat - q_lo x SE, with SE = SD_null/C_R; >= 20000 replicates x 5 families. SIMULATION RULE AT A GIVEN kappa (stated here in words; analyze_a.py implements it from this text and shares no code with the producer's tools; it is the rule EXP-PFDR-011cd0's analyze_relcensus.py applied in code): on each simulated curve the structured-arm count is first drawn from the G-NB-R null model of that curve; for kappa > 1 a Poisson-planted excess (compound-planted where a clause names it) is added to that draw; for kappa = 1 the null draw is used as drawn; for kappa < 1 the null draw is binomially thinned -- each of its relations is kept independently with probability kappa, so the count is Binomial(null draw, kappa) -- and no excess is added. The rule applies wherever this experiment simulates a structured count at kappa_hat or at kappa = 1.00: the U_A simulation above, every synthetic design of the coverage simulation below (including the kappa = 1.00 point, whose synthetic designs are null draws and whose own bounds are computed by this rule), the |dev| fallback below, and the P0 and RA-05 predictions of U_A and of its coverage. One-sided coverage of U_A is simulated at kappa = 1.00, 1.10 and 1.15 (>= 4000 synthetic designs each) and printed beside U_A as "one-sided 95% (signed quantile), simulated coverage x.xxx". If any of the three simulated coverages is below 0.945, the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 A-INT |dev|-quantile bound governs instead, labelled "quantile of |dev|, simulated one-sided coverage x.xxx". The |dev| bound is reported beside U_A in every case. When kappa_hat < 1 the labels read "one-sided 95% (signed quantile; kappa_hat < 1, binomial thinning), simulated coverage x.xxx" and "quantile of |dev|; kappa_hat < 1, binomial thinning, simulated one-sided coverage x.xxx", and the bound is read as "no excess detected", never as kappa_rel < 1.
analysis.X_rel: Smallest kappa on the grid 1.00, 1.01, ..., 1.30 with simulated P(z > t_dec) >= 0.5 at the realised n, Poisson-planted and compound-planted (A-arm dispersion 1.307 x D) beside each other; the larger is reported. A design sensitivity, never a realised bound (EV-PFDR-ad6274 INF-4). If no grid point reaches simulated power 0.5 for a planting, that planting's X_rel is recorded as "X_rel > 1.30" with no value, and the reported (larger) X_rel is then "X_rel > 1.30"; the grid is not extended. "X_rel > 1.30" exceeds 1.15 wherever an outcome condition compares X_rel: with z_A <= t_dec it assigns O-A4; with z_A > t_dec X_rel enters no outcome condition and is reported only. The same rule applies to the predicted X_rel of P0 and of RA-05.
analysis.dispersion_robustness: rho_A = D_A_hat / D_R_hat with D_A_hat = [sum_j (d_j - (kappa_hat - 1) nbar_j)^2 - sum_j s_j^2/3] / sum_j nbar_j (red team J4 d), curve-cluster bootstrap 95% interval; z_A recomputed with V x max(1, upper end). If the outcome class depends on it, the outcome id carries the flag dispersion-sensitive; routing is unchanged.
analysis.per_rung: Per rung b: kappa_b, z_b and per-rung calibrated p for small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, planted_target and the null pseudo-cells. Secondary; the only per-rung quantity used anywhere is the sign of small_x's kappa_30 - 1 and kappa_32 - 1, as a routing qualifier.

gates.text: RA-02, on the EC-A1 build: re-run the two archived EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 jobs 4-b30-c10 and 4-b32-c10 with the exact commands in experiments/EXP-PFDR-011cd0/runs/RUN-PFDR-011cd0-table/attempt-1/jobs/4-b30-c10/command.txt and .../4-b32-c10/command.txt (output paths moved under this experiment's run directory); after gzip decompression and JSON parse, every census row (timing keys excluded, as EXP-PFDR-011cd0 G1'), every harvest row and every staircase row equals the archived rows.jsonl.gz, harvest-rows.jsonl.gz and staircase.jsonl.gz of the same job; then the same two jobs with --arms extended by planted_sub and small_x_offset give identical rows for every pre-existing arm. Comparator reproduce_check.py only.

analyze_a.py's recount (CC-1 to CC-3) of the archived R12 TT4 random-arm and known-null relation counts reproduces calibration.json PC_NULL.known_null_band_cells["known_null_sub|TT4|band"].C_R and .sum_s2 as integers: 3 x C_R and 6 x sum_s2, each rounded to the nearest integer, are equal for the recount and for the archived values; no float is compared for equality. Both are integer-valued by construction: 3 x C_R is the total of the three random arms' counts over the curves, and 6 x sum_s2 is the sum over curves of 3 x (sum of the three squared counts) - (sum of the three counts)^2, because each ddof-1 variance of three integers is a multiple of 1/6. From the archived values 1035.0000000000095 and 1049.333333333356 the expected integers are 3105 and 6296 (planning approximation (hand): 3 x 1035.0000000000095 = 3105.0000000000285 and 6 x 1049.333333333356 = 6296.000000000136); P0X-A compares against the archived file as read at RA-03, not against these figures.

coordination/design/TASK-20261002-729fc9.gate_rule: Any failure of G-REPRO, P0X-A, G-FRESH, G-T, G4, G4-R, G7, G7-OFFSET, G-CURVE, G-REL or PC-R-iii makes the affected run invalid and nothing downstream is read (O-A-INVALID). A failure of PC-NULL-R, PC-R-T (i) or (ii) or PC-R-D, with every invalidating gate passing, leaves the structural reading INCONCLUSIVE (O-A-UNCAL); the H1c TT4 and H4 readings stay readable.

outcomes.note: Pre-registered before any data; "replicates" means pooled z_A > t_dec. O-A1, O-A1b, O-A2, O-A3 and O-A4 are evaluated only when every invalidating gate and every control passes and small_x keeps at least 80% of each rung's design curves after CC-6, that is, only when neither O-A-INVALID nor O-A-UNCAL applies; exactly one of them is then assigned. M (small_x_offset) is admitted on a design curve unless that curve is removed from M by the height screen (controls_design_notes.offset_range_and_height_screen) or by CC-6 (unmatched size of small_x_offset, or failed_infrastructure of small_x_offset or of any arm of the family it is scored with on that curve); "M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves" counts, at each rung, the design curves on which M is admitted against design.json's final n_b. A timeout, crash, memory or disk stop is failed_infrastructure or a checkpoint, never a negative reading. Status changes, if any, are made only by a later Coordinator decision after independent review.

rows.condition: any invalidating gate fails
rows.meaning: nothing is read; the run returns to the executor with the defect named; never evidence about small_x TT4

rows.condition: invalidating gates pass; PC-NULL-R, PC-R-T or PC-R-D fails; or fewer than 80% of a rung's design curves remain after CC-6 for small_x
rows.meaning: structural reading INCONCLUSIVE; the failing control is analysed in review before any redesign

rows.condition: z_A > t_dec; kappa_30 > 1 and kappa_32 > 1 for small_x; M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves; z_M <= t_dec; z_Delta > t_Delta
rows.meaning: The excess replicates at both rungs and is lost under the base mutation: a small_x-specific relation-source CANDIDATE. No reading, no status change, no synthesis (TW-ALIVE). Routed to a review-breakthrough round at max with an independent replication, S_3-to-solution measured there (the remaining observation collision: an informative but solve-useless homogeneous excess).

rows.condition: z_A > t_dec and the case is neither O-A1 nor O-A2 (M admitted on fewer than 80% of some rung's design curves; or M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves, z_M <= t_dec, and either one rung's small_x kappa <= 1 or z_Delta <= t_Delta)
rows.meaning: A replicated small_x excess whose specificity the mutation (or the rung split) does not resolve. TW-ALIVE as O-A1, with the review asked to design a sharper mutation; no reading.

rows.condition: z_A > t_dec and z_M > t_dec, with M admitted on at least 80% of each rung's design curves
rows.meaning: The excess replicates and persists under the mutation: NOT small_x-specific; attributable to the consecutive-x construction, the engine or the size matching. Because two structured arms then exceed matched randoms on fresh curves, it is still a TW-ALIVE event under H-PFDR-2765d2's falsification conditions: review (instrument audit first: G-REL, planted recovery, arm-order and table-construction effects) before any reading.

rows.condition: z_A <= t_dec, U_A <= 1.15 and achieved X_rel <= 1.15 (a grid value; "X_rel > 1.30" never meets this)

stopping_rules: Order is fixed -- RA-01; RA-02; RA-03 (design.json pinned); RA-04; cross-run checks; RA-05 (calibration.json pinned); RA-06.

If P0X-A or G-FRESH fails or P0 reaches a design stop -- stop before RA-04 and return.
A certificate or row-verification failure (G4, G4-R) stops that run at once; the run is invalid; rows so far are retained.
A per-instance, per-job or address-space stop ends that instance or job as failed_infrastructure; others continue; no re-run except a per-run watchdog continuation of unstarted or killed jobs.

No adaptive sampling beyond the pre-data P0 rule. No optional stopping. Blinding before RA-06, in the EXP-PFDR-011cd0 I-7 form: RA-05 parses no count of small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup or planted_sub (I-A7); and every check run in RA-04 or between RA-04 and RA-05 (G4, G4-R, G-CURVE, G-REL, G7-OFFSET, PC-R-iii), which reads structured and planted rows where the fixed order (stopping_rules [0]) places it, emits for the structured and planted arms (small_x, small_x_offset, subgroup, planted_sub, planted_target) only per-instance PASS/FAIL and mismatch keys -- never a relation count, row count, total, kappa or z -- to any log or file before RA-06 (instance counts by status are not such counts). A mismatch key identifies where a check failed and nothing else: the check id, run, job, bits, c, arm, m, mode, class and the name of the compared field (for example relations_distinct, R_star, x0 or the planted vector); it may not contain either compared value, their difference, a count, a total, a kappa or a z.
TW-DISK checkpoints the task; never a result.

pareto_honesty.dominated_by: Pollard rho (about 0.886 sqrt(N) group operations, O(1) memory; internal: H-PFDR-2765d2 asymptotic_claim.prior_best) for every outcome of this engine. This experiment claims no attack and no speedup; a constant kappa_rel cannot move this engine's exponent N^{max(h, m-h+1)/m} (0.75 at m = 4, internal), and nothing here measures growth with N.
pareto_honesty.sota_delta: No attack; a measurement contribution only. Resolution on small_x TT4 relation-level kappa improves from SE 0.0361 at 4000 curves (U 1.171, not excluding 1.15) to a planned SE of about 0.0277 at 6800 fresh curves (planning approximation), with a mutation contrast that EXP-PFDR-011cd0 did not have.

interpretation_limits: A non-detection bounds this one cell at 30-32 bits on these curves and this engine; it closes nothing by itself and says nothing about growth with N.
A replicated excess is a lever candidate for review-breakthrough and independent replication, not a result and not a speedup.
The mutation separates small x-height from chance and from consecutive-x structure only within its own power; a non-discriminating mutation is reported as such (O-A1b).
Toy scale; generated curves; no deployed-curve statement.

experiments/EXP-PFDR-0b3699/specificatio.objective: Decide, with one pre-registered test, whether the small_x TT4 relation-level excess seen in EXP-PFDR-011cd0 (kappa_rel 1.0966183574879125, one-sided bound 1.1711499549303037 above the 1.15 target, excess concentrated in the 32-bit rung; EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4) is chance or a small_x-specific relation excess, on fresh prime-order curves at 30 and 32 bits, this mitm engine at default arity and min_fill, m = 4, class TT, with |F| matched to the subgroup base. Sensitivity at the target is shown by a planted arm at kappa about 1.15 (RC-2); the threshold is checked against a real-data permutation null (RC-3). REAL-DATA PERMUTATION NULL (RC-3; red team PTM2 (b)) -- per curve, the four null arms' counts exchanged uniformly at random, position 0 scored against positions 1-3 by CC-8; its 0.99 quantile t_perm reported beside G-NB-R's t_A; the larger governs (t_dec)

SECONDARY STRUCTURED COMPARATOR -- subgroup (F_sub), scored against the same randoms; never decision-bearing for Part A
BASELINE REPRODUCTION -- G-REPRO (archived EXP-PFDR-011cd0 R12 rows reproduced on the EC-A1 build) and P0X-A (the archived 011cd0 TT4 random-arm C_R and sum_s2 recounted from archived rows)

controls_design_notes.mutation_choice_and_justification: Chosen before any data: the offset mutation, not small_x on the quadratic twist. The twist E' has order 2p + 2 - N, in general composite: it leaves the prime-order generator, the N-prime setting of Lemma L1 (red team PTM-L shows L1 failing at composite N) and the calibrated CC-8 null, and it changes the group, the targets and the base-size rule. The offset keeps every one of those and changes exactly one property: whether the consecutive x-coordinates are small integers (low height) or sit at a random place in F_p. It separates the three explanations: chance (neither small_x nor the mutation shows an excess on fresh curves), a small-x-specific source (small_x does, the mutation does not, and the paired contrast is positive), and an interval, engine or size artefact shared by consecutive-x bases (both do).
controls_design_notes.offset_range_and_height_screen: x0 is drawn in [p/4, 3p/4) so the walk neither wraps nor touches the small_x interval. Rationals of small height (for example (p + 1)/2 + k = (2k + 1)/2) can still fall inside the walk with small probability, so before any census run design_a.py lists every curve whose offset base contains an x with x * v mod p in [-2^12, 2^12] for some v in 1..16; such a curve is dropped from the mutation arm and from the contrast only (CC-6-style listed exclusion), never from the primary test.
controls_design_notes.planted_target_construction: planted_sub plants, at m = 4 and 30-32 bits, exactly one TT relation F_d = F_a + F_b - F_c' per curve (n_tt = max(1, round(s^4 / (6 N))) is 1 there: at bits 32, curve 10, s_sub 209 and N 2839806169 give s^4/(6N) about 0.11, a planning approximation (hand)) plus one TB relation. The planted relations, with indices and signs, are written in the base's params. planted_target counts every relation of planted_sub on curves in S, and on curves outside S every relation except that curve's planted TT monic vector, removed by exact match. The planted excess is therefore exactly K_plant relations, located on declared curves of a real planted base. If a planted TT vector is absent from its curve's relation set on ANY curve, PC-R (iii) fails and the run is invalid. K_plant per rung b = round(0.15 x n_b x mu_b) with mu_30 = 521.3333333333334/2000 and mu_32 = 513.6666666666666/2000 (the smallx-tt4-localise.json C_R fields); at the declared n_b = 3400 this is 133 and 131, a planning approximation (hand); the P0 run computes the exact values. S is the first K_plant_b curves of random.Random(f"plant-target|EXP-PFDR-0b3699|{b}").sample(curves_b, n_b), recorded in design.json before any census run.
controls_design_notes.why_planted_target_is_new: EXP-PFDR-011cd0's planted arm sat far above the target (TT3 kappa about 1.50, TB3 about 4.79; OBJ-RT-2), so its pass showed dynamic range, not sensitivity at 1.15. RC-2 requires sensitivity at the target; at the declared n the predicted detection of kappa 1.15 by z > t_dec is about 0.999 (planning approximation (hand): (1.15 - 1)/SE with SE about 0.0277 is about 5.4 null SDs), so a miss is a calibration failure.

preregistered_prediction.quantity: kappa_rel(small_x, TT, m 4) pooled over fresh 30-bit and 32-bit curves (c in the Part A range), with z_A, and the same for small_x_offset and the paired contrast.
preregistered_prediction.formula: Null (pre-committed): HEUR-2765d2-H2, kappa_rel = 1 + O(N^{-1/2+eps}), so E[C_A] = E[C_R] to well below SE and P(z_A > t_dec) <= 0.01 by construction of t_A (one-sided 0.01); the planning SE at the declared 6800 pooled curves is about 0.0277 (planning approximation (hand): 0.03613980068046521 x sqrt(4000/6800)). Alternative carried from EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4: kappa_rel about 1.097. The design is sized for power 0.90 at kappa 1.10 (power_analysis.target); its power at kappa 1.097 at the final n is computed by P0 (power_analysis.P0_rule steps (3) and (5)) and recorded in design.json before any census data, and no value of it is asserted here; both are powers at a post-selection estimate (power_analysis.target). Coordinator prior, recorded before any data of this experiment and after reading EV-PFDR-ad6274 (exposure as draft_meta): O-A3 0.80; O-A4 0.02; a replicated excess (O-A1, O-A1b or O-A2) 0.13 in total (O-A1 0.05, O-A1b 0.04, O-A2 0.04); O-A-UNCAL or O-A-INVALID 0.05.
preregistered_prediction.source: H-PFDR-2765d2 HEUR-2765d2-H2 (random-model justification: complete mixed character sums cancel because Hom(E, G_m) = 0 -- recalled, supports nothing; incomplete-sum regime outside the proven range per Shparlinski 2008, abstract retrieved by TASK-20260928-9c44f2); Lemma L1 (derivation tier for TT under U, DEC-20261002-c3f49b na8_ruling_L1) for the first two moments of the null relation count; the alternative's size from EV-PFDR-ad6274 OBS-4. Frozen at approval; any change is an additive protocol_amendment and never re-scores a run.

scale_relevance.justification: Generated prime-order curves at 30 and 32 bits (max log2 p = 32: toy by the mechanical rule cited in EV-PFDR-ad6274 claim_tier_basis), one engine (mitm, arity 2, min_fill), m = 4, class TT. No transfer or extrapolation is asserted: nothing about N above 32 bits, growth with N (Part C), other cells, other bases, other engines or deployed curves (TW-SCOPE).
